title: Staggered kernel warmup causing multi-deployment TTFT variance — telemetry bridge & emergency mitigations
creator: Sofia Patel
description: Multiple enterprise customers reported intermittent TTFT regressions and sustained tokens/sec degradation across Hosted, Dedicated, and Private clusters starting 2026-03-09. Initial triage implicated a staggered kernel warmup path introduced in runtime-1.20 that delays kernel vectorization for mid-length sequences when multiple model variants are loaded concurrently, causing serialization at the scheduler and a cascading increase in first-token latency for multiplexed requests.
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Deploy a multi-variant model fanout with two quantized variants (int8 + int4) and one fp16 variant. 2) Send 50 parallel short prompt requests (<= 40 tokens) with mixed routing weights to the same model route and observe first-token timing. 3) Ramp to 200 concurrent sessions with burst traffic pattern (3s spikes). 4) Compare first-byte and tokens/sec across warm nodes and cold-start nodes. Expected: consistent TTFT distribution. Observed: 2-3x TTFT skew on ~25% of requests and tokens/sec drop on affected workers.
impact_summary: - Customers: 3 enterprise customers with SLO breaches reported (finance/health verticals).  - Symptom: elevated first-token latencies (median +120ms, p95 +400ms) and 20-40% reduction in sustained tokens/sec under multiplexed load.  - Scope: Hosted regions us-west1/us-east1, Dedicated clusters with mixed-variant pinning, and Private VPC installs where runtime-1.20 was applied.  - Business: SLO alerts, support escalations, and one open escalation with account team requesting immediate mitigation and post-mortem.
timeline: 2026-03-09 11:20 UTC: first customer alert received; 2026-03-09 12:00 UTC: on-call triage assigned (S. Patel); 2026-03-09 15:30 UTC: initial kernel warmup hypothesis formed; 2026-03-10 09:00 UTC: reproducer validated in staging; 2026-03-11 02:00 UTC: emergency mitigation (warmup fast-path) staged for canary; 2026-03-12 05:00 UTC: canary rolled to 10% hosted traffic — mixed results; 2026-03-14 22:00 UTC: expanded telemetry, added per-kernel timers; 2026-03-15 08:30 UTC: prepping release runtime-1.20.3-hotfix
mitigation_actions: - Immediate: enable deterministic kernel preselection on affected pools (config flag runtime.kernel_preselect=true) to avoid staggered warmup. - Short-term: apply a per-deployment override for kernel warmup window (runtime.warmup_window_ms=150) on sensitive customers. - Medium-term: backport optimized vectorization check that avoids serializing scheduler when mixed quantization is present. - Communication: notify affected customers with ETA and mitigation steps; provide temporary config snippet for self-hosted Private clusters.
rollback_plan: If hotfix introduces regressions: 1) flip runtime.kernel_preselect=false and restore previous warmup behaviour; 2) revert runtime-1.20.3-hotfix to runtime-1.20.2 on canary nodes and monitor p95; 3) if Dedicated/Private customers applied the flag locally, provide assist script to undo and validate kv cache integrity.
monitoring_playbook: - Dashboards: runtime/ttft-by-kernel, runtime/tokens-per-sec-by-worker, scheduler/queue-depth. - Alerts: p95_ttft > baseline +300ms for 5m => page on-call. - Runbooks: run kernel-timers collector (scripts/run_kernel_timers.sh) and capture 'kernels.log' and 'sched.trace' from affected workers. - Validation: post-deploy smoke: 500 concurrent short prompts for 10 minutes, assert tokens/sec within 10% of baseline and p95_ttft < baseline +150ms.
decision_log: - 2026-03-10: Decided to avoid immediate full rollback due to risk of moving back to less-optimized kernel path; opted for deterministic preselection flag as safe guard. - 2026-03-12: Canaries showed partial improvement; added more granular per-kernel sampling. - 2026-03-14: Product approved runtime-1.20.3-hotfix release candidate pending final test matrix.
